newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey puts state banks on sale.
newsitem.headline: Turkey puts state banks on sale.

text.p: Turkey put three state banks on sale on Monday as first part of the government's ambitious privatisation plan, the Privatisation Administration (OIB) said.
It said the fully state-owned Etibank was split into three banks to form Etibank, Denizbank and Anadolubank to make the sell-off easier for buyers.
Buyers will submit their bids, to be in dollars, by December 16 to the OIB. The OIB will negotiate with bidders, which can go for either one, two, or all of the three banks.

The privatisation of Etibank and its two offshoots is seen as a key step to implement the government's sell-off plans, which has so far raised $3.1 billion since 1986. The OIB plans $5.9 billion in privatisation revenues in 1997.
The sale of the three banks is expected to bring in about $100-150 million, according to analysts.
Etibank has a paid-in capital of 2.3 trillion lira and 124 branches in Turkey, and Anadolubank and Denizbank each has one trillion lira of capital and three branches.
